Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

yourhonor 0.0.0.9000 (development version, unreleased)

Initial development version. Nothing has been released; the list below is the feature set as it stands, and the “Review fixes” section records what changed during the pre-release code review so that early adopters can update their calls.

Features

  • calibrate_judge() compares judge labels with one or more human raters. A live judge sees only the columns listed in input_cols; human columns and judge_col are rejected as inputs. Items are shuffled before grading and keyed with a fresh opaque .item_id; keyed output is validated and restored to source order. With several raters the reference label is the modal consensus, ties are excluded and counted, and human-human reliability is reported as a benchmark rather than a ceiling.
  • agreement() reports Cohen’s kappa, Krippendorff’s alpha, and Gwet’s AC1 (nominal) or AC2 (weighted) with item-bootstrap intervals, a fixed label universe, explicit missingness, and an explicit status for degenerate data. Zero-width bootstraps at empirically perfect agreement are flagged unreliable rather than reported as certainty.
  • confusion() and confusion_metrics() give the confusion matrix in declared label order plus per-class support, precision, and recall with exact intervals; plot_confusion() draws the matrix with ggplot2.
  • probe_bias() runs pointwise verbosity, self-preference, and bandwagon probes in one blind, randomised batch. probe_position() swaps structured candidate columns into neutral display slots and maps choices back to stable candidate identity. combine_bias() merges probe evidence under one multiple-comparison family. All three report raw missingness and conservative directional intervals.
  • test_retest() re-grades items and reports mean pairwise disagreement with a hybrid bootstrap/Wilson interval, chance-corrected stability, and an any-flip rate that is explicitly tied to the number of runs.
  • acceptance_policy() makes thresholds explicit, including sample-size, class-support, missingness, probe, and stability requirements. report() turns the evidence into PASS, FAIL, NOT_ASSESSED, or INDETERMINATE and is descriptive only when no policy is supplied.
  • audit_vitals() and stability_vitals() reuse grades and epochs already present in a vitals task without another model call; stability_vitals() refuses epochs whose judge-visible content changed. write_audit() writes a Markdown report or a versioned JSON summary (yourhonor.audit.v1) that omits item rows.
  • support_gold is an eight-item synthetic dataset for API demonstration.
  • synthetic_gold is a 200-item synthetic dataset with three simulated raters, sized so an audit can reach a verdict; it drives the README’s end-to-end run and the vignette. Every label is planted and the text is templated.

Review fixes

User-visible changes made while addressing the pre-release code review.

Calibration edge cases (#1)

  • A calibration whose human (consensus) reference uses a single category now reports status = "insufficient_reference_variation" for every coefficient instead of an estimate: Gwet’s AC1 read “almost perfect” there while kappa read zero.
  • Agreement tables gain conf_low_exact, a resampling-free finite-sample lower bound on each coefficient’s own observed agreement (irrCAC’s weighted pairwise pa), mapped onto the coefficient’s scale. It is Clopper-Pearson for two raters without weights, a binomial stop-loss bound for kappa, AC1, AC2 and two-rater alpha otherwise, and for alpha with three or more raters a relative-entropy bound on its rating-weighted ratio. Near misses earn their weighted credit, so the bound approaches the estimate as items grow for weighted and multi-rater coefficients too. Policies assess the smaller of it and the bootstrap conf_low on every sample; on a perfect sample the bootstrap interval is a zero-width point at 1, so the exact bound decides there, and a perfect sample is no longer INDETERMINATE where one error could PASS. Small-n bootstrap optimism no longer reaches a decision. For kappa and alpha on imbalanced labels the bound is weak (it is divided by 1 - pe) and usually decides the check below a few hundred items.
  • Chance agreement now counts only the categories some rater used, so declaring an unused level no longer moves Gwet’s AC1. Weights still follow the full declared scale, so under weights an unused level still enters the chance term (linear AC2 on levels 1-3: pe 0.55 with three declared levels, 0.70 with a fourth). Beyond the observed levels it leaves kappa’s and alpha’s estimates unchanged but lowers their conf_low_exact. This applies to test_retest() too.
  • ci_reliable also requires at least 30 finite resamples, so an n_boot below 30 can never give a reliable interval; the documentation now says so.
  • calibrate_judge() reports judge abstentions (an NA judge label on an item with a human reference) separately from human gaps: n_judge_abstentions, judge_abstention_rate, and its Clopper-Pearson interval. acceptance_policy(max_abstention_rate = ) bounds the interval’s upper end. The encoding is documented under “Missing labels and abstentions” in ?calibrate_judge.
  • acceptance_policy()’s coefficient now defaults to NULL, the calibration’s Gwet coefficient (AC1 nominal, AC2 ordinal); the old "gwet_ac1" default left an ordinal calibration NOT_ASSESSED. When the calibration did not compute that Gwet coefficient (for example coefficients = "cohen_kappa"), the agreement check is NOT_ASSESSED and the rest of the report is still assessed. Naming a coefficient the calibration did not compute is an error at assessment.
  • The JSON artifact adds calibration.confusion (long-form counts), calibration.per_rater_agreement, and the abstention fields.

Labels and blinding

  • Ratings are integer-coded before they reach irrCAC, which upper-cases, trims, and blanks character labels internally. Labels that differ only by case or whitespace now stay distinct in every coefficient and in test-retest stability, matching confusion(). Empty or whitespace-only labels are rejected everywhere with a request to use NA instead.
  • Inferred label universes union declared factor levels with every label observed in a non-factor column, so confusion() no longer silently drops a pair whose label is absent from a factor’s levels.
  • Blind grading strips element names and free-form attributes from every judge-visible vector, list element, record field, and nested frame, closing a channel through which a column built with sapply() over labels or IDs carried them to the judge row-aligned through the shuffle. Structural attributes (class, levels, tzone, units, dim, ptype) are kept; S4 objects, environments, and functions inside list columns pass through as is.
  • Calibration results keep both key spaces: items$.item_id is the source-row key and items$.judge_item_id is the key the judge saw. cal$blinding_map maps between them and cal$judge_output is keyed by both. test_retest() returns a parallel judge_item_ids matrix. Join judge-side logs on the judge key, never on the row number.
  • A judge that returns a factor declares its own label universe; those levels are kept when label_levels is NULL. stability_vitals() likewise uses a factor score_col’s levels so declared-but-unobserved labels count toward chance agreement.

Agreement and confusion

  • agreement() and confusion() gain explicit column arguments (rater_cols; human_col and judge_col). Without them, columns named human and judge are used when both exist; otherwise agreement() treats every column as a rater and confusion() reads a two-column frame positionally and errors on wider frames. Any inferred choice that ignored or positionally read columns is reported with a message of class yourhonor_inferred_columns. plot_confusion() forwards ... to confusion().
  • coefficients now defaults to NULL in agreement() and calibrate_judge(), meaning kappa, alpha, and AC1 with AC2 substituted for AC1 under weights. Explicitly requesting "gwet_ac1" with weights is an error rather than a silent substitution.
  • agreement(<calibration>) inherits every stored setting (coefficients, conf_level, n_boot, seed, label_levels, weights) for arguments left at their default, so agreement(cal, n_boot = 50) keeps the stored seed and confidence level. One set of bootstrap resamples is shared by all coefficients within a call.
  • plot_confusion() keeps the declared label order on both axes instead of sorting alphabetically; confusion() attaches the resolved order as the "label_levels" attribute.
  • print() for a calibration shows each coefficient’s interval and interpretation; the interval was previously dropped.
  • The modal-consensus rule for multiple raters, its exclusions (n_consensus_ties, n_insufficient_human_ratings, n_excluded), and its optimistic direction are documented in ?calibrate_judge.

Bias probes

  • probe_bias() and probe_position() return one shared schema (32 columns) built by a single constructor, so pointwise and position rows can always be combined. n_missing and pair_missing_rate are renamed n_unscored and unscored_rate; n_items_missing (items with at least one NA judgment) and n_directional_items are reported for every probe. The evidence and item_evidence attributes are lists named by probe on every object; combine_bias() concatenates them without nesting.
  • probe_position() counts an item toward the directional sign test only when it was decided in both display orders and its canonical choice moved with the order, so abstaining on one order no longer reads as a position preference. A tie counts as a decided judgement that commits to neither slot. The directional rate and interval use scored items as the denominator, as the pointwise probes do.
  • A probe with no label movement now enters the multiple-comparison family with p_value = 1 instead of NA; p_value is NA only when status == "insufficient_data", and combine_bias() recomputes verdicts.
  • flip_threshold is now a practical-significance floor on the net directional_rate, not on the any-direction flip_rate: a large but balanced flip rate is reported but never flagged "BIAS".
  • The directional interval’s upper bound is capped at the flip-rate upper bound over the same denominator, since the net rate can never exceed the any-direction rate.
  • probe_bias() aborts when input is not a character column or contains NA; a pasted NA would otherwise be graded as a real answer and hide abstention from the missingness gate.

Stability

  • The pairwise-disagreement interval is documented as a hybrid: the percentile item bootstrap widened to a Wilson score interval for the mean per-item disagreement. It can only widen. The chance-corrected estimate and its stability_status are derived from the same filtered matrix, and the label universe for the coefficient comes from every run.

Policy and report

  • report() always returns a visible yourhonor_report list with decision, checks, and the supplied evidence; output only sets the default print rendering. Use x$decision instead of attr(x, "decision"), and format(x, output = "md") or as.character(x) for the Markdown lines.
  • checks gains numeric value and threshold columns and an op column (">=", "<=", "lower >=", "upper <=", "="); the old prose threshold string is gone. Each required probe yields up to four checks (bias_<probe>, _direction, _missing_rate, _n), and printed check lines show value (op threshold).
  • acceptance_policy() rejects a stability or probe threshold supplied without its gate (max_pairwise_disagreement or required_probes), so a policy can never carry a threshold the assessment does not read. Those errors and probe-name errors carry class yourhonor_policy_error. Every required argument is checked with rlang::check_required().
  • Validation errors name the caller’s argument (for example n_boot, ordered_levels, choice_levels) and the calling function rather than an internal helper.
  • The report’s bias summary distinguishes required probes from probes supplied outside the policy, and mentions descriptive signals in the latter.

vitals adapters and artifacts

  • audit_vitals() uses score_col directly as the judge-label column, so cal$judge_col, cal$items, and the JSON provenance no longer contain an internal sentinel name. It aborts when the samples already contain a human_col column instead of overwriting it, and validates provenance.
  • write_audit() gains overwrite = FALSE; an existing file is an error unless overwrite = TRUE. JSON is written at full precision (digits = NA), every absent value is null (never {}), vector-by-contract fields (label_levels, coefficients, required_probes, adapter input_cols and human_cols) are always arrays, class-specific min_recall and min_precision are objects keyed by class, created_at is RFC 3339 UTC (2026-01-31T12:00:00Z), and checks carries value, op, and threshold. The schema is documented in ?write_audit.

Second review pass

  • Validation messages that name unknown labels (agreement(), confusion(), calibrate_judge(), test_retest(), stability_vitals()) render again instead of failing inside cli; absent explicit columns are pluralised, and the label-universe minimum names the actual count (one for agreement and confusion, two for calibration).
  • Printed check lines raise their precision until the value and threshold differ, so a FAIL at 0.1005 against 0.1 no longer reads = 0.1 (<= 0.1). checks$value is always the quantity op compares and is NA when the interval is untrusted; the reason then names the cause (a boundary-degenerate bootstrap, too few finite resamples, an unavailable or reversed interval) rather than echoing status = "ok".
  • A required probe smaller than min_probe_n is again INDETERMINATE under bias_<probe> with its interval unassessed, rather than a possible FAIL. A probe or calibration at another confidence level withholds only its interval checks (bias_<probe>_missing_rate and _n, usable_items, calibration_missing_rate, and class_support are still assessed). A duplicated coefficient row or an empty class-metrics table is reported as INDETERMINATE or NOT_ASSESSED instead of being read silently.
  • acceptance_policy() rejects an orphan threshold with a readable sentence, and every validation error it raises carries class yourhonor_policy_error.
  • The console report prints every class line and the n of N judge-evidence line that the Markdown report already had (and, like the Markdown report, tolerates a calibration without class metrics), and a non-required probe whose verdict is INCONCLUSIVE is mentioned in the bias summary whether or not the policy names required probes. A check value and threshold that only part beyond 15 significant digits are printed exactly.
  • agreement(<calibration>, weights = ...) re-resolves the inherited coefficients under the new weights instead of treating the stored Gwet variant as an explicit, conflicting request. confusion() and confusion_metrics() reject human_col/judge_col on a calibration object as agreement() rejects rater_cols; confusion_metrics() applies label_levels to a calibration’s or confusion tibble’s stored metrics; frames with duplicated column names are refused; the positional-inference hint names both selectors; and errors from confusion_metrics() name it and say whether a calibration object or a confusion tibble was passed. A count above the integer range (for example n_boot = 1e10) is rejected with a message naming that bound.
  • The bootstrap draws one resample per iteration, shared by every requested coefficient, instead of materialising an n x n_boot index matrix, and draws nothing when no coefficient is estimable.
  • combine_bias() carries over only evidence for probes present in each constituent’s rows, so stale evidence left by row-subsetting cannot shadow a newer run, refuses an unnamed evidence list instead of emptying it, and names given to ... no longer prefix the evidence names. probe_position() reserves .judge_item_id, display_choice, and canonical_choice; probe_bias() validates id_col on the full data before sampling.
  • Structured judge output returning a .judge_item_id column is rejected, and judge_output$label is always character. test_retest() unions a judge’s factor levels with every label observed across runs, and an unused blank factor level is dropped from inferred levels (test_retest(), stability_vitals()). stability_vitals() documents that level inference applies to unweighted runs only.
  • write_audit() writes doubles with 17 significant digits so they round-trip exactly, refuses a directory as path, and the calibration provenance uses the same RFC 3339 created_at as the top level with NULL adapter fields (id_col, audit_id) present as null. provenance must have unique, non-blank names. Any task whose $get_samples is callable is accepted by the vitals adapters.

Third review pass

  • calibrate_judge() without label_levels infers the label set from the human and judge labels together (with factor levels), so a label only the judge used no longer aborts; supplied label_levels are still enforced.
  • A structured judge may return .item_id as the exact string form of the issued key; any other key gets the package’s own error instead of a vctrs one.
  • agreement() and calibrate_judge() reject a repeated coefficient.
  • interpret_agreement() bands now match Landis and Koch exactly: 0 is "slight", not "poor".
  • agreement() on all-missing ratings now says there are no non-missing ratings instead of blaming label_levels.
  • The acceptance policy’s bias flip-rate and directional checks now count every unscored probe item (a missing judgment, or a position item lost to a within-condition tie across repeats) as a worst-case flip in their upper bounds. A weakly position-biased judge could previously pass at the default repeats = 2 because its bias landed in ties; it now reads INDETERMINATE. Unscored items never cause a FAIL, and fully scored probes are assessed exactly as before.
  • probe_position() documents that even repeats can tie, and that taking the mode attenuates a per-call bias.
  • conf_low_exact is now capped at the bound of the perfect samples a sample can be corrected into, so a judge is never assessed above a judge that matches the human reference on the same items. The cap costs most at small n with rare categories; coverage is unchanged. Inversions between two imperfect samples remain possible, since correcting an error can lower the estimate itself.
  • The write_audit() documentation says that “full precision” refers to the stored doubles: irrCAC rounds each coefficient to five decimals.
